title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 106 (Restriction on voting rights)

content.overview: Section 106(1) permits a company's articles to restrict voting on shares registered in a member's name where calls or other sums presently payable on those shares remain unpaid, or the company has exercised a right of lien over them. Under section 106(2), a company cannot prohibit a member from voting on another ground. Section 106(3) allows a member entitled to multiple votes on a poll to use fewer than all of them and to cast the votes used differently.

content.study:
## Section 106 — restriction on voting rights

**Subsection (1): unpaid calls or lien.** The articles may provide that a member cannot exercise voting rights in respect of shares registered in that member's name if calls or other sums presently payable by the member have not been paid, or the company has exercised a right of lien over the shares.

**Subsection (2): no other ground.** A company may not prohibit a member from exercising voting rights on a ground outside subsection (1). The statutory text says “a company”; this rule must not be rewritten as applying only to public companies.

**Subsection (3): use of votes on a poll.** A member entitled to more than one vote—or a proxy or other person entitled to vote for the member where permitted—need not use every vote and need not cast all votes used in the same way.

## Apply the provision
- Identify the shares registered in the member's name and the voting right in issue.
- For subsection (1), establish unpaid calls or other sums presently payable, or a company lien exercised over the shares; do not infer a restriction from a general disagreement with the member.
- For subsection (2), test whether the asserted prohibition is based on one of the grounds specified in subsection (1).
- For subsection (3), distinguish entitlement to multiple votes from the member's choice about how many votes to cast and how to cast them on a poll.

Section 106 should be read with the meeting and poll provisions where relevant, including sections 107 and 109. This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Subsection (1): unpaid calls or lien
sections.body: The articles may provide that no member shall exercise voting rights in respect of shares registered in the member's name on which calls or other sums presently payable by that member have not been paid, or in regard to which the company has exercised a right of lien.

sections.heading: Subsection (2): restriction on other grounds
sections.body: A company shall not, except on the grounds specified in subsection (1), prohibit a member from exercising voting rights on any other ground.

sections.heading: Subsection (3): multiple votes on a poll
sections.body: A member entitled to more than one vote on a poll, or a proxy or other person entitled to vote for the member where permitted, need not use all available votes or cast all votes used in the same way.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 106 (Restriction on voting rights)

examples.title: Unpaid call on registered shares
examples.body: A member has shares registered in their name and has not paid a call that is presently payable on those shares. If the company's articles contain a restriction permitted by section 106(1), the member's voting right in respect of those shares may be restricted on that statutory ground. This is an educational illustration, not advice about a real dispute.

examples.title: Member with multiple votes on a poll
examples.body: At a poll, a member entitled to five votes chooses to cast only three and casts those three differently on the questions put. Section 106(3) says the member need not use every vote or cast all votes used in the same way. This is an educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: The articles purport to suspend a member's voting rights solely because the member criticised the board. No unpaid call, other presently payable sum, or exercised lien is identified. How should section 106 be analysed?
hypotheticals.analysis: First identify the precise ground for the restriction. Subsection (1) identifies unpaid calls or other sums presently payable, and a company lien exercised over the shares. Subsection (2) prohibits a company from barring voting on another ground. On the stated facts, the board's disagreement with criticism does not itself match either subsection (1) ground. Confirm the articles, share register, payment records and any asserted lien before reaching a conclusion.

hypotheticals.question: A member is entitled to four votes on a poll but wishes to cast only two, one for and one against the resolution. Does section 106(3) require all four votes to be used together?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Subsection (3) states that the member need not use all votes and need not cast all votes used in the same way. Apply the rule to the actual voting entitlement and poll procedure, and check any other applicable statutory or procedural requirements.

distinctions.right: Section 107 — voting by show of hands; section 109 — demand for a poll

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 106(2) as a restriction applicable only to public companies.
misconceptions.correction: The subsection says “a company”; do not add a public-company limitation absent from the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming any unpaid amount, dispute or disagreement automatically suspends voting rights.
misconceptions.correction: Identify calls or other sums presently payable on the shares, or a right of lien exercised by the company, and check the articles and facts.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a member entitled to multiple votes must cast all votes and cast them identically on a poll.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (3) says the member need not use all votes or cast all votes used in the same way.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 106 regulate?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 106(1) permits articles to restrict voting on shares where calls or other sums presently payable remain unpaid, or a company lien has been exercised. Subsection (2) bars prohibitions on other grounds. Subsection (3) lets a member entitled to multiple votes on a poll leave some votes unused and cast the votes used differently.
